what: PR #120 CodeQL path injection findings in recovery/evidence probes
expected: CLI arguments cannot select evidence write locations or inject path separators into historical log names.
observed: Before the fix the real probe created a caller-selected directory and the archived phase expression returned traversal input unchanged.
root_cause: The recovery probe passed argv[3] through resolve into mkdir and multiple writeFile calls, and called realpath(argv[2]) before establishing its temporary-root boundary. The archived probe interpolated argv[2] without restricting phases.
fixed_by: Allocate evidence with mkdtemp instead of accepting an output path; normalize/check the temporary app boundary before realpath and validate the canonical result; select archived phases from literal before/after/smoke returns. Run regressions in the CI security suite. Native ordinary/prepared recovery matrices and prepush passed. A subsequent CodeQL run cleared alerts 80-84 and reported alert 85 at the normalized lookup. Select the lexical/canonical temporary alias first, then use one dominating containment check before realpath. Both aliases, all rejected path cases, ordinary/prepared source recovery and the required prepush gate pass again. No finding was dismissed or rule disabled.

invariants: Evidence directories are freshly created and owned by the probe
External, sibling-prefix, temporary-root and escaping symlink app arguments are rejected
Archived log phases are literal before/after/smoke values
Ordinary and prepared reload recovery, previous-generation HTTP and joined shutdown still work

limitations: The archived probe contains historical machine-specific setup and moved imports. Its actual phase declaration is extracted with the TypeScript parser and evaluated directly for all accepted phases and traversal inputs; the entire historical app experiment is not rerun.
Native runtime replay uses a disposable cloned installed minimal app. The existing e-commerce preview is left running and is not edited.
GitHub CodeQL/CI results are checked separately on the published final commit; no alerts are dismissed or scanning rules disabled.

Alert 85 was reproduced as an actual failing CodeQL analysis. No additional runtime path escape was observed: all original rejection cases already passed on 45f69537f. The follow-up expresses the same dual-alias policy as one dominating containment guard.

The full dotenv/source matrix in recovery-after.log was run for the first repair. After the guard-only follow-up, both temporary aliases are checked natively and the canonical-path ordinary/prepared source matrix is rerun with --source-only. Dotenv/compiler/runtime implementation is unchanged by either PR review repair.

notes: Historical before/after application logs remain unchanged; only the executable archived probe phase selection is hardened.

Regression tests were initially authored under packages/cli/tests/dev-environment/paths.test.ts, then moved to tests/security/dev-recovery-probe-paths.test.ts so the standard CI security gate executes them.

The actual hosted CodeQL failure is retained before the follow-up. The query's primary-source StartsWithDirSanitizer and RelativePathStartsWithSanitizer were inspected; no suppression, dismissal, query exclusion, or output waiver was added.
